Image size & uploads / FIELD GUIDE

How to crop a photo to square, portrait or landscape

An image can have the right shape without looking squeezed or losing the details that matter.

By Manglo Editorial7 November 20266 min read
THE MANGLO PLAYBOOK / ORIGINAL GUIDE

Profile photos, product cards, stories and video thumbnails often use different shapes. If you upload the same image everywhere, the website might cut off the subject automatically. Taking control of the crop lets you decide what stays in the frame.

Common aspect ratios explained

RatioShapeExample use
1:1SquareSquare avatar or product thumbnail
4:5PortraitTall feed image
16:9LandscapeWide banner or video-style image
9:16Tall portraitStory-style visual

These are popular shapes, not guaranteed specifications for every platform. Always check the destination's current rules before exporting.

Crop and resize are different actions

Cropping removes part of the outside image to change framing or proportions. Resizing changes how many pixels the remaining image has. If a landscape photo must become square, crop first. Do not simply change its width until everything is distorted.

Crop using Manglo

  1. Choose a clear original image and keep a copy untouched.
  2. Open the Manglo cropper and upload it.
  3. Select square 1:1, portrait 4:5, landscape 16:9 or story 9:16.
  4. Use the position controls to keep the most important subject in view.
  5. Export, inspect the final frame and resize separately if a pixel limit is specified.

Keep the subject where it belongs

For an identification or application photo, follow the issuing organization's exact composition instructions. For product photographs, avoid cropping off handles, accessories or visible condition details. For a portrait, leave enough space around the face that the destination's own thumbnail crop will not remove part of it.

Three easy mistakes to avoid

  • Stretching: changes the subject's real shape.
  • Over-tight framing: leaves no breathing room around a product or face.
  • Wrong final dimensions: a square crop may still be too large or too small in pixels.

Once the crop is right, use the resizer to fit pixel dimensions or the target-size compressor for a KB limit. The best workflow changes only what the destination requires.
